title: Sebastian and the Veil
premise: Zephyrine Delacroix has spent nine years as the crown's food-taster, swallowing small poisons so the king doesn't have to, and keeping his head down in a kingdom where the old gods were outlawed a generation ago. When prayers start being answered again—first his own, whispered over a dying friend—the gods' return cracks open the truth that Thornfell was never a country at all but a prison, and its royal family are wardens who fed on the gods' captivity. Hunted by both the crown and the desperate faithful, Zephyrine must gather a found family of smugglers, ex-priests, and one very inconvenient princess to find the Veil-door out of a country that will cease to exist when the last god escapes. In the end he chooses loyalty over survival: he holds the door open for everyone else, loses his memories of them to pay the toll, and wakes on the far side as a stranger—until the found family crosses after him and chooses to remember him first.
about_author: Odile Sandoval is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who swears the best plot ideas arrive during service rush. They write fantasy about people whose jobs are smaller than their destinies.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine tasting goes wrong when a dish carries a poison no apothecary recognizes—one that tastes, impossibly, of lightning. He survives it alone, hiding the symptom: he briefly hears a voice say his childhood name. Emotional beat: loneliness established; the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. His dying mentor, old smuggler Brannoc, asks Zephyrine to pray at a roadside shrine as a joke. The prayer is answered; Brannoc's fever breaks by morning. Zephyrine realizes the outlawed gods are waking—and that his immunity-building has made him a vessel they can speak through. Beat: awe tangled with terror.

chapters.title: The Warden's Daughter
chapters.summary: Princess Isolde's POV. Isolde discovers her father burning maps of places she's never heard of and interrogates the palace archivist, learning the royal family's true role as wardens of the Veil. She begins secretly investigating. Beat: dutiful daughter starts becoming a traitor to her inheritance.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Fleeing the capital before the crown connects the poison to him, Zephyrine uses his knowledge of Thornfell's hidden passes to reach the mountain shrine-roads, guided by the voice—now named: Vess, a minor god of thresholds. Beat: reluctant partnership with something divine.

chapters.title: The Company of the Broken Bell
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He falls in with a smuggling crew: one-eyed captain Maret, defrocked priest Osk, and twin forgers Pip and Tam. Their bell-shaped talisman is cracked—a relic of the silenced gods. They need a taster who can detect divine poison. Beat: found family begins, prickly and transactional.

chapters.title: What the King Ate
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde finds her father's private ledger: every 'poisoning attempt' he survived was staged, each one feeding the wardens' power. Her brother Corvin knows and has chosen the throne over the truth. Beat: betrayal inside the bloodline; Isolde flees the palace.

chapters.title: Lightning in the Wine
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The crew raids a warden supply cache; Zephyrine tastes the cargo and channels Vess fully for the first time, seeing the Veil itself—a membrane around Thornfell, thinning as the gods wake. The country is a jar with a loosening lid. Beat: scale shift from personal to cosmic.

chapters.title: Corvin's Hunt
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Crown prince Corvin leads soldiers into the mountains, ordered to kill the 'vessel.' But Corvin privately fears what his father is, and hesitates at the shrine-road ambush. Beat: antagonist with a conscience; the hunt becomes a chase.

chapters.title: The Shrine at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde, disguised, reaches Hollowmere shrine seeking answers and collides with Zephyrine's crew. Osk recognizes her despite the disguise. Tense standoff; Maret votes to ransom her; Zephyrine vouches for her. Beat: two storylines braid together; trust risked.

chapters.title: Toll of Memory
chapters.summary: Vess speaks through Zephyrine (his POV, half-dream). To open the Veil-door, someone must pay a toll in memory—and the door only opens from inside a country that must stop existing to let anyone leave. The crew argues about who pays. Beat: the cost made explicit; loyalty tested in theory.

chapters.title: The Burning of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, mostly Zephyrine's. Corvin's soldiers burn the shrine; the crew saves the villagers but Osk is captured covering their retreat. Isolde reveals herself to her brother to bargain for Osk's life—and fails. Beat: first real loss; guilt lands on Zephyrine.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Priest
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. Tortured in a mountain fort, Osk refuses to name the crew but learns the king plans to re-seal the Veil by sacrificing every awakened god—and every vessel, including Zephyrine. He escapes with help from an unlikely guard. Beat: stakes sharpened; endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: The Map That Eats Itself
chapters.summary: Pip and Tam's POV (alternating). The twins discover the old road-maps redraw themselves as the Veil thins—Thornfell is literally forgetting its own geography. Villages are vanishing from memory and record. Beat: dread through detail; the country is already dying.

chapters.title: What I Swallowed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Nine years of poisons surface as visions: he relives every dish, every death he may have caused by surviving. Vess offers to take the memories as partial toll. Zephyrine refuses—he'd rather hurt than forget. Beat: character keystone; defines the ending choice.

chapters.title: The King's Table
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde returns to the capital under parley and dines with her father, who offers her Corvin's place beside him if she betrays the vessel. She sees what he truly is: something wearing a king. She poisons his cup with the same lightning-toxin—and he doesn't die. Beat: horror peak; the mask slips.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Forgetting
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reunion and flight toward the Veil-door at Thornfell's heart as whole valleys unwrite themselves behind them. Corvin intercepts—not to kill Zephyrine, but to beg him to close the door and save the people still inside. Beat: antagonist becomes ally; impossible choice framed.

chapters.title: Maret's Price
chapters.summary: Maret's POV. At the door's threshold, Maret reveals she's been to it before—as a child, paying the toll that took her eye's memory of her mother's face. She claims the right to pay again, full price this time. The crew fights over who goes. Beat: love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Climax part one: the king arrives, unsealed and monstrous, to force the Veil shut forever. Vess burns through Zephyrine to hold the door; the land dissolves around the battle. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, the crew holding the threshold against the dark.

chapters.title: Loyalty Over Truth
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Climax part two: Zephyrine realizes the door needs a warden's blood willingly given—but instead of sealing it, he turns the rite inside-out, unmaking the wardenship. The king unravels; Corvin and Isolde renounce the throne aloud. Beat: the theme resolved in action, not speech.

chapters.title: The Toll Paid
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The door opens only if someone stays to hold it until the last refugee crosses. Zephyrine volunteers, paying the full memory-toll. One by one the crew passes through, each trying to make him remember them as they go. Beat: heartbreak engineered across ten chapters, paid off.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Far Side
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. On the other side, Zephyrine wakes blank among strangers in a green country under an open sky. Isolde watches him not know her name. Then Maret steps forward and says, 'You're ours. We'll do the remembering.' Beat: grief transmuted into chosen belonging.

chapters.title: Sebastian
chapters.summary: Ensemble epilogue, mostly Zephyrine's. Months later, the refugees build a village; the freed gods pass through quietly, and Vess leaves a small door in Zephyrine's garden gate. When asked his name, he says 'Sebastian'—the one thing the toll couldn't take, because the crew wrote it on his hand before he crossed. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
